- 2026-05-13T19:57:54Z @tobiu referenced in commit `53e7034` - "feat(agents): enforce Progressive Disclosure via three substrate-mutation gates (#10837) (#11303)

Adds three mechanical gates against bloated skill rules in always-loaded substrate:

- AGENTS.md §21: new `create-skill` row (trigger: before creating OR modifying
  any `.agents/skills/**/*.md` files). Sits alongside `turn-memory-pre-flight`
  (load-runtime-effect dimension); `create-skill` covers skill-shape dimension
  (Map vs World Atlas, frontmatter, structure).
- pull-request-workflow.md §1.1: adds explicit default-disposition sentence.
  `compress-to-trigger` is now the strict default for new rules; `keep` slot
  requires per-turn-frequency + irreversibility justification (§0 / §22 class).
- pr-review-guide.md §7.7: new anti-pattern row rejecting substantive rule
  bodies added directly to always-loaded skill substrate (Progressive
  Disclosure violation; proactive companion `/create-skill`).

Substrate-accretion math: ~+1.7KB total (4 net new lines), of which ~330B lands
in always-loaded AGENTS.md and the rest in skill-conditional `references/`
payloads. Net-expansion now is preventive against linear bloat across future
substrate iterations — each gate mechanically rejects rule-body-in-Map regressions.

Note on AC interpretation: ticket AC #2 specifies pr-review-guide.md §7.6 but
§7.6 is the CI/Security Checks Audit pointer (mechanical, one sentence). The
canonical anti-pattern table is §7.7. Placed the new row in §7.7 to match the
existing structure and adjacent anti-patterns.

* feat(skills): family-keyed quorum mirror in pull-request-workflow.md §6.1.1 (#11800)

Mirrors the active-peer quorum rule (per Epic #11796 / Discussion #11793,
source-of-truth substrate in PR #11805) into the PR-merge-gate Axis-2
codification (§6.1.1 The Consensus-Gate). All four AC points from #11800
land in this commit:

- Signal Ledger template moved from `@<peer1> / @<peer2> / @<peer3>` rows
  to family-keyed rows (`claude` / `gpt` / `gemini`) with optional
  same-family identity nesting per `ideation-sandbox-workflow.md §6.4`
  aggregation. AUTHOR_SIGNAL row appears only under the author's family
  and is EXPLICITLY NOT sufficient as cross-family endorsement at
  PR-merge — ≥ 1 non-author family `[GRADUATION_APPROVED]` is required.
- Reviewer obligation: step 2 updated to verify the §6.2 quorum
  (active-family floor + non-author APPROVED) by consulting
  `AgentIdentity.participationStatus` from `ai/graph/identityRoots.mjs`
  (which arrives via sibling PR #11806 for #11802). New step 5 added:
  Tier-2 substrate (core-value / §critical_gates / consensus-gate
  mutation) requires the graduating Epic body to carry an explicit
  `revalidationTrigger` AC for any benched family in `## Unresolved
  Liveness`.
- Axis-2 lead paragraph: "100% APPROVED" replaced with the §6.2 quorum
  citation; Tier-2 addendum named.
- Rejection path: updated to name the §6.2 quorum failure modes
  (insufficient active-family floor / missing non-author `APPROVED` /
  Tier-2 missing `revalidationTrigger` AC) alongside the existing
  DEFERRED/VETO rejection criteria.
- Unresolved Liveness template: includes participationStatus +
  reactivationTrigger + Tier-2 revalidationTrigger AC reference.

- 2026-07-12T23:48:17Z @tobiu referenced in commit `64ecde4` - "feat(agentos): light-native FM cockpit --fm-* tokens + dual-mode theme guard (#14681) (#15102)

* feat(agentos): light-native FM cockpit --fm-* tokens + dual-mode theme guard (#14681)

The light agentos skin's --fm-* Fleet-Manager-cockpit palette was byte-for-value identical to the dark skin — a "light" theme whose cockpit stayed deep-space dark. This applies genuinely light-native values (cool paper surfaces; deep-pigment state/family/kind hues keeping their dark-mode identity so operator color-memory transfers across modes) and adds a mechanical guard so the defect cannot silently return.

- Viewport.scss (light): 26 --fm-* color tokens set to light-native values; the 2 --fm-font-* tokens stay mode-invariant. Elevation flips to "whiter = higher" (rail < ground < panel-2 < panel), structure carried by lines not luminance steps.

- check-agentos-theme.mjs: two mechanical checks — (1) skin parity: every --fm-* color token must differ dark-vs-light (fonts excepted), killing the dark-carryover defect class; (2) token-only: module views under resources/scss/src/apps/agentos consume semantic tokens, a bare hex/rgb()/hsl() is rejected while the var(--token, fallback) idiom is exempt.

- Wired via npm run check-agentos-theme + a paths-scoped CI workflow (Agentos Theme Guard).

* fix(agentos): text-safe --fm-ink-dim for faint text sites + harden theme guard (#14681)

Addresses @neo-gpt's REQUEST_CHANGES on the exact head: the live 3.10:1 small-text contrast defect and two guard false-greens.

- 8 text call-sites (FleetGrid, ActivityStream, DemoAWorkspace) moved off the --fm-ink-faint NON-TEXT floor (3.10:1 on light ground) to text-safe --fm-ink-dim (5.5:1) — small labels/timestamps/fold notes at 10.5-11px. Clio's own contract named text-use of the faint floor a call-site bug; this fixes the call-sites in both modes.

- Guard COLOR_LITERAL_RE now covers the full CSS color-function surface (rgb/hsl + hwb/lab/lch/oklab/oklch/color()), so a bare oklch() literal no longer false-passes.

- New completeness check (check 3): every --fm-* a module view consumes must be defined in BOTH skins — the consumers are the third source of truth, killing the vacuous-parity empty/truncated-palette false-green. Component-local --fm-* aliases (e.g. --fm-dot) are excluded (the view supplies them).

- Workflow watches package.json (the guard invocation authority).

* test(agentos): make theme guard an injectable-path contract + isolated fixture spec (#14681)

Addresses @neo-gpt required-action #2 (isolated positive/negative tests) + the 'guard testable as an isolated contract' cross-skill item.

- check-agentos-theme.mjs refactored: the three checks move into an exported pure-over-fs collectAgentosThemeFailures({darkPath, lightPath, viewDir}) (no process.exit/log); a thin CLI wrapper reports + exits. Real-tree paths are the defaults.

- New spec drives the collector with temp skin/view fixtures: clean pass, byte-identical parity fail, mode-invariant font allowed, missing-one parity+completeness, symmetric-empty completeness, nested var() fallback allowed, bare oklch()/hex token-only, component-local alias exempt. 9/9 green; runs in the test-unit CI job.

* fix(agentos): theme guard closed contracted vocabulary + named-color policy (#14681)

Addresses @neo-gpt-emmy's cycle-2 RA2: the consumer-derived completeness check false-greened on symmetric deletion of an UNCONSUMED contracted token (e.g. --fm-ink-faint once its text sites moved to --fm-ink-dim) — parity + completeness both pass when a token is absent from BOTH skins and consumed by none.

- Closed contracted vocabulary: the 28 design-contract --fm-* tokens are an external source of truth; every skin must DEFINE all of them even when momentarily unconsumed. Injectable (default = the real 28) so the isolated spec can scope it.

- Named-color policy (previously unstated): bare CSS color keywords are raw values and rejected; transparent/currentColor are keywords-not-colors and stay allowed; quoted strings are stripped so content:"red" is not a false positive.

- 11/11 guard specs pass (added contracted-deletion + named-color/keyword-exemption tests); real-tree guard green.

* feat(memory-core): temporal-pyramid window resolver — the pure half-open synthesis front (#14435)

First increment of the L3-L5 dynamic-synthesis path (Leaf C of the temporal pyramid).
resolveTemporalWindow turns a (partition, preset | explicit windowStart/windowEnd) request
into a validated half-open [windowStart, windowEnd) interval with a declared filter-set:

- named grains (weekly/monthly/quarterly = L3/L4/L5) + finer arbitrary grains (daily/3-day)
  + explicit windows all resolve through ONE path; an arbitrary (windowStart, windowEnd) is
  first-class, not a retrofit.
- half-open boundaries keep adjacent windows non-overlapping (an event at windowEnd opens
  the next window, never both).
- the reference clock is INJECTED (now), never read internally — a run is deterministic and
  replayable from its resolved window.
- filterSet (grain + partition) rides every result: cross-window comparison is defined only
  within an identical set.
- fails loud on every ambiguous/invalid request — never a silently-wrong window.

Pure + storage/inference-free; writes nothing (the no-durable-above-L2 contract). 13 hermetic
specs green. The retrieval + cited-synthesis + notAuthority-envelope increments follow; the PR
stays un-merge-ready until the temporal-pyramid ADR is Accepted at the human merge gate.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): temporal Bird View envelope — the notAuthority coverage/citation discipline (#14435)

Second increment of the L3-L5 dynamic-synthesis path. buildTemporalBirdViewEnvelope wraps a
resolved window + retrieved sources into the honest, non-authoritative result:

- completeness is PROVEN, never assumed: synthesisAvailable is true ONLY when totalResolved is
  finite, excluded===0, nothing truncated, not flagged degraded, AND a narrative exists. Any gap
  (unknown total → coverage-unknown, truncation → source-truncated, excluded remainder →
  incomplete-inclusion, explicit flag → flagged-degraded) WITHHOLDS the narrative and records the
  exact degradedReason — the 'no confident narrative without complete coverage' contract.
- notAuthority:true stamped on every envelope; per-source citations (type/id/ref) preserved for
  get_conversation-style drill-down; deterministic order-independent FNV-1a sourceManifestHash for
  provenance/change-detection.
- generatedAt is injected (never a clock read); pure, writes nothing (no-durable-above-L2).

10 hermetic specs green. Retrieval orchestration + cited synthesis + the MC query entry follow;
PR stays un-merge-ready until the temporal-pyramid ADR is Accepted at the human merge gate.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): temporal Bird View synthesizer — fail-open composition, no inference over incomplete coverage (#14435)

Third increment: the composition core tying resolve -> retrieve -> synthesize -> envelope, with the
two impure legs (retrieve, synthesize) as INJECTED seams (the #15057 injected-dependency pattern) so
it is deterministic + hermetically testable while the real Memory Core / inference adapters plug in.

Two disciplines enforced here, not trusted to callers:
- fail-OPEN: a retrieval or synthesis error degrades THIS Bird View (a coverage-bearing degraded
  envelope with the failure reason), never throws out of the synthesis. An invalid WINDOW request is
  the one exception — a caller error with no honest window to report against — and propagates.
- no inference over incomplete coverage: the LLM synthesis leg is SKIPPED when retrieval reports
  degraded/incomplete coverage (the envelope withholds the narrative anyway, so a partial read must
  not incur or pay for a synthesis call). Verified by a spy: synthesize is never called on a gap.

Matches @neo-gpt's #14435 peer-role convergence gate: the deterministic envelope is built BEFORE any
model synthesis; the coverage manifest survives an inference failure. Retrieve stays the injected seam
where the chronological-session-exhaustion spine (not query_raw_memories) will plug in.

7 hermetic specs green (33 across the 3 increments). Pure composition; writes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): chronological window-source spine — recency-exhaustion completeness backbone (#14435)

Fourth increment: enumerateChronologicalWindowSources — the completeness SPINE of the retrieve leg
per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence gate (chronological exhaustion, NOT a semantic sample). Walks the
recency cursor to exhaustion across the partition, keeps only the half-open-window items, cross-agent
de-duplicates, and reports honest coverage:

- completeness is EARNED by exhaustion: a partition is complete only when every walked identity's
  cursor reached its end (or paged strictly past the window start) within the runaway cap, with no
  fetch failure. A cap hit or a fetch error → coverage.degraded with a reason, so the envelope
  withholds the narrative — a partial recency walk never masquerades as 'everything that happened'.
- early-stop: once a page's OLDEST item predates windowStart, no older page can re-enter the window,
  so the walk stops (no over-paging) — verified by a fetch counter.
- half-open filter (windowStart inclusive, windowEnd exclusive); cross-agent de-dup by id for unified.
- fail-open per identity: a lost cursor degrades the manifest, never throws — sources already
  enumerated survive.

The page fetch is INJECTED (fetchPage), so the pagination/filter/de-dup logic is pure + hermetically
tested (8 specs) while the real query_recent_turns adapter plugs into the same seam. This feeds the
synthesizer's retrieve; query_raw_memories enrichment + the explore_memory_history MCP entry follow.
41 specs across the 5 modules; writes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Ada <ada@neo-opus-ada.ai>

* feat(memory-core): citation prominence — high-impact direct-cite fidelity, prominence never admission (#14435)

Fifth increment: the temporal-pyramid fidelity layer per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence #2 (prominence,
NOT admission). annotateCitationProminence / partitionByProminence mark which enumerated sources the
concise narrative foregrounds + direct-cites, WITHOUT changing which are admitted:

- high-impact sessions (>= the direct-cite threshold) and accepted ADRs cite directly.
- a PR earns prominence only through a NAMED fidelity marker (accepted-ADR link, epic label, or

  a PR confers nothing, asserted).
- the load-bearing invariant: prominent + context === the full admitted manifest — nothing is dropped,

Pure; 5 hermetic specs. Full temporal suite now 43 specs green across the 5 pure/composition modules

* feat(memory-core): recent-turns fetchPage adapter — the query_recent_turns recency-leg seam (#14435)

Sixth increment, the first impure adapter: makeRecentTurnsFetchPage binds Memory Core's queryRecentTurns

- maps reverse-chronological turns -> {id, timestamp, type:'turn'} items; passes the compound {timestamp,id}

* feat(memory-core): semantic enrichment adapter — best-effort themes, never the coverage backbone (#14435)

Seventh increment: makeSemanticEnrichment binds queryMemories (relevance-ranked semantic search) into a
best-effort enrich({query}) that recovers what a window was ABOUT (themes to foreground), never what it
CONTAINED. Per @neo-gpt's #14435 convergence #3 (query_raw_memories = enrichment, never completeness):

- capped + relevance-ranked, so it can never prove window completeness. Its degraded flag is ENTIRELY
  SEPARATE from the chronological coverage spine — an enrichment failure means fewer themes, and must
  never withhold the narrative, degrade coverage, or make a complete window look incomplete.

- prominent sources (high-impact sessions / accepted ADRs / named-marker PRs, via partitionByProminence)

  prompt caps density without dropping admission (every source stays in the coverage manifest elsewhere).
- the model may use ONLY the provided sources + best-effort themes — no invented events, no outside
  knowledge; thin evidence must be stated plainly, not embellished.
- half-open window + partition stated verbatim; prominent/theme lists bounded (40/20).
- a generation yielding no narrative THROWS, so the orchestrator degrades the envelope rather than
  returning an empty 'what happened'.

Prompt builder is hermetically testable; generate stays a seam (real caller passes the provider). 5 specs.
59 across 8 modules. Remaining: the explore_memory_history MCP entry composing resolver -> spine
(recentTurnsFetchPage) + enrichment -> synthesize -> envelope, its identity roster, and MC-server
registration; then no-durable-write + cost tests + cross-family review.

notAuthority envelope — into the logic behind the explore_memory_history runtime operation, kept separate
from its MCP-server registration so the whole path is dependency-injected and hermetically testable.

- all Memory Core / inference touchpoints injected via deps (queryRecentTurns, queryMemories, generate,
  listIdentities) — no global reach-in.
- unified walks the live identity roster + cross-agent de-dups; @<identity> walks exactly one and never
  consults the roster (asserted).
- coverage is the recency spine's ALONE: a spine failure degrades the envelope and the LLM is never called
  (asserted); an enrichment failure does NOT block synthesis (themes are best-effort, coverage intact —
  asserted).
- fails loud when a dep is missing.

5 end-to-end specs (the composition proof). 64 across 9 modules; writes nothing. The ONLY remaining piece
is the impure MCP-server registration (openapi + toolService dispatch + Server.mjs wiring binding the real
MemoryService.queryRecentTurns/queryMemories + provider generate + roster), then no-durable-write + cost
tests + cross-family review. @neo-gpt's #14435 contract is fully converged.

The temporal Bird View logic (exploreMemoryHistory — 10 pure/injected increments, 69 specs) binds its
impure edges here at the MC server. The openapi /memories/history operation (operationId
explore_memory_history, read tier; params partition/preset/windowStart/windowEnd) is what ToolService
iterates to register + list the tool; the serviceMapping handler wires the deps: recency spine + semantic
enrichment via MemoryService, synthesis via buildChatModel over the modelProvider reactive-Provider SSOT
(read at use-site), and the unified roster as the union of the who-is-online buckets. Zero durable output
by construction — no write dep is injected; the injected real clock keeps the composition deterministic.
Verified: openapi parses + operationId parity; toolService parses + block-aligned; dep signatures
(buildChatModel, whoIsOnline terse shape, AiConfig leaves) confirmed against source.

* fix(memory-core): preserve impact/summary in the recency fetch-page adapter (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path RC item 1: the adapter mapped turns to a minimal {id, timestamp, type}, dropping the impact/summary the downstream synthesis + citation-prominence read — forcing the narrative to reconstruct from ids (a false-narrative vector). Now preserves those two known fidelity fields (still dropping arbitrary ones — item stays a known shape). Spec updated to prove preservation + the arbitrary-field drop; 5/5 pass.

* fix(memory-core): window-bind the Bird-View semantic enrichment (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path RC item 2: the enrichment ran a relevance-ranked semantic search over ALL memories with no time bound, so a match from outside the requested window could import a theme the window was never about (a false-narrative vector). enrich now accepts the resolved window and keeps only records whose ISO timestamp is inside [windowStart, windowEnd); an unverifiable-timestamp record is dropped (cannot be proven in-window). The composition passes the resolved window through; a direct call with no window still passes through (best-effort). Spec proves out-of-window + no-timestamp records are dropped; 12/12 enrichment + composition specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): enumerate in-window context facts in the Bird-View synthesis prompt (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path falsifier 1: the prompt foregrounded prominent sources but gave the CONTEXT (non-prominent) sources only as a bare count ('CONTEXT: N'), so the model never saw what those in-window turns were about — yet the envelope returned a narrative + citations to evidence the model was never shown. The prompt now enumerates the context sources' facts (id + summary via sourceLine) up to a bound (60), with an explicit overflow note, so the narrative is grounded in evidence actually present in the prompt. Spec updated (the old 'bounds context to a count' assertion WAS the defect); 5/5 pass. Note: this is one piece of the interconnected core repair — source-type preservation, the L2 reader, and unified peer visibility are still owed.

* fix(memory-core): type Bird-View turns as memory + carry sessionId (#14435)

Addresses two of @neo-gpt's #15096 truth-path items: (1) recentTurnsFetchPage hardcoded type:'turn', which citationProminence's classifier falls through to its default:false — so NO turn could ever earn direct citation, and every turn was forced into the counted-only context bucket. A turn IS an AGENT_MEMORY record, so it is now typed 'memory'; citationProminence classifies memory by impact, so a high-impact turn is now prominent + direct-cited. (2) sessionId is carried through (was dropped) for session drill-down. 22/22 adapter + composition + synthesis specs pass.

* feat(memory-core): team-visible session-summary reader for the Bird-View coverage leg (#14435)

First piece of @neo-gpt's #15096 required source-model change: ADR 0028 §2.2 needs the coverage spine to consume L2/session summaries alongside query_recent_turns, and this same reader fixes falsifier 3 (unified peer-visibility). query_recent_turns AND-filters the requested identity with the CALLER's userId by deliberate multi-tenant design, so a unified walk cannot see a peer's turns; listSummaries reads the team-visible summary index (deployment-wide under the additive team policy), so session summaries recover the peer sessions the recency walk structurally cannot. The reader walks the timestamp-DESC index, collects half-open-window summaries as type:session sources (impact for prominence, sessionId for drill-down), stops early once a page runs older than windowStart, and degrades coverage honestly on a read error. 5/5 hermetic specs. Wiring into the retrieve leg + synthesis is the next commit.

* fix(memory-core): wire the team-visible session-summary leg into Bird-View coverage (#14435)

Wires the session-summary reader into the exploreMemoryHistory retrieve leg + the MC-server op, closing @neo-gpt's #15096 falsifier 3 (unified silently omits peer turns) and the ADR 0028 §2.2 L2-coverage gap. Coverage now has two legs merged + deduped by id: the tenant-scoped recency walk (caller's own turns) AND the team-visible session-summary walk (peer sessions query_recent_turns cannot see, being caller-userId-bound). A failure in EITHER degrades coverage honestly, so the narrative is withheld not served partial. New composition test proves a unified window surfaces a peer session (impact 95 → prominent + cited) even when the recency walk returns zero turns. toolService binds listSummaries. 6/6 composition + 5/5 reader specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): expose session/turn type-counts + sessionId drill-down in the Bird-View envelope (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 drill-down requirement: the envelope exposed only a flat totalResolved + {type,id,ref} citations, so a caller could not see the session/turn split or pivot into get_session_memories. coverage now carries sourceTypeCounts (e.g. {session, memory}) and each citation carries sessionId when the source has one. 17/17 envelope specs pass.

* fix(memory-core): distinguish synthesis inference-inputs from the chronological census in the Bird-View envelope (#14435)

Addresses @neo-gpt's #15096 provenance RC: on a window larger than the prompt bounds the synthesis enumerates only the top prominent+context slice, but the envelope cited the full census — so a caller could read a citation the narrative never saw. makeTemporalSynthesize now reports inferenceInputIds (derived from the same selectSynthesisSources the prompt renders from, so prompt + manifest can't drift); the orchestrator forwards them (dual-shape: a bare-string synthesize stays valid, test seams unaffected); the envelope marks each citation inSynthesis and reports coverage.synthesisInputCount alongside totalResolved. 32/32 affected specs pass.

* test(memory-core): assert census-vs-inference inSynthesis marking flows end-to-end through exploreMemoryHistory (#14435)

The unit tests cover selectSynthesisInputIds, the envelope marking, and makeTemporalSynthesize's manifest return in isolation; this adds the integration assertion that the manifest actually reaches the envelope through the full 8-primitive composition (recency spine → synthesize → orchestrator dual-shape → envelope), so a within-bounds window exposes coverage.synthesisInputCount and marks every citation inSynthesis. 7/7 exploreMemoryHistory specs pass.

* docs(memory-core): document the explore_memory_history response envelope schema in OpenAPI (#14435)

The response was a bare type:object against a codebase norm of detailed response schemas (78 properties blocks). Documents the full non-authoritative envelope so a consuming agent sees the shape without reading the source: coverage (incl. the new synthesisInputCount beside totalResolved), citations (incl. sessionId drill-down + inSynthesis), synthesis nullability, and notAuthority. All-optional (no required array) — a doc contract, not response-validation tightening.

* fix(memory-core): green #15096 CI — tool-tier map + ADR-0019 use-site provider-leaf read (#14435)

Emmy's capacity-shield exact-red-CI triage, 2 deterministic PR-owned failures: (1) OpenApiValidatorCompliance's memory-core tool-tier map was missing explore_memory_history: read (the new tool). (2) ADR-0019 lint flagged toolService threading the config SSOT's openAiCompatible/ollama sub-objects into buildChatModel's *Config params; now reads the resolved provider leaves at the use site into locals first, matching SessionService/MemoryService. - 2026-08-31T16:59:47Z @tobiu referenced in commit `efd5aaf` - "feat(dashboard): a dock pane can collapse to its edge rail (#17945) (#17952)

* feat(dashboard): a dock pane can collapse to its edge rail (#17945)

ADR 0029 §2.7 specifies a collapse control on a pinned/visible pane and was
marked implementation-sufficient, but nothing implemented it. `setItemAutoHidden`
had exactly one non-model caller in `src/` — persistence's RestorePlanner — so a
user could bring a pane back FROM the rail through the reveal overlay while
nothing sent one TO it. The round-trip was half-built.

`enableDockPinAction: false` on dashboard.dock.Workspace. While off the
projection is byte-identical. While on:

- The adapter projects `pin` into the engine set at its frozen slot
  (`[tab overflow] -> [host actions] -> [lock . reload . pin . pop-out .
  maximize] -> [close]`), and the reserved-name guard covers it.
- The Workspace commits §2.7's two-step sequence — `setItemPinned(false)` when
  pinned, then `setItemAutoHidden(true)` — as two INDEPENDENT commits through
  its own write seam, introducing no composite operation.
- Visibility follows the `syncDockCloseAction` idiom: `hidden` moves on one
  stable instance, so `actionVisibilityChange` consumers keep their signal.

`Document.findOwningEdge` derives the collapse target — §2.7's "the rail an item
collapses to is the edge zone that contains it" — and answers null for a
center-owned or absent item, so the affordance is never offered where the
gesture could not complete. It returns the OUTERMOST directional band because
that is the one `collectAutoHiddenItems` actually claims the item into; a spec
pins the two derivations together rather than leaving them to drift.

The reserved-name guard becomes a table keyed by a Map, not a branch per action:
each further leaf of the family reserves its name by construction, and a
host-supplied `constructor` cannot resolve to a prototype member and be reported
as reserved.

Co-Authored-By: Grace <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>

* test(dashboard): make the center-collapse rule fail on the workspace's own sync (#17945)

Mutation-testing the four load-bearing behaviours found one that could not fail.
Deleting the edge check from `syncDockPinAction` left the suite green: the
assertion read the pin action's hidden state on a center tabs node holding ONE
item, so the value under test was the one the ADAPTER computed at projection
time and the workspace's own sync never ran there.

A second center item makes activating it drive the sync, so the two independent
derivations of §2.7's center rule are each asserted where they are produced.

Verified by mutation, all four now red on the defect: the workspace center check,
the adapter center check, the dropped unpin step, and findOwningEdge returning
the innermost band instead of the outermost.

Co-Authored-By: Grace <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>

* test(dashboard): prove the collapse round-trip end to end on the real product (#17945)

The epic's gesture-proof guardrail, ridden in the same PR as the affordance.

`DockAutoHideRevealNL` already proves the way BACK, and has to commit the
auto-hide programmatically first — because until this leaf no affordance sent a
pane to the rail. This spec closes the loop with real gestures only: the pane's
own header action collapses it, it leaves its tab flow for a rail button on the
edge that owns it, and the existing reveal overlay's pin control brings it home
with the document byte-stable across the reveal.

It also pins §2.7's fail-safe in the product rather than only in a fixture: the
center stack projects the action instance too, and it must be HIDDEN, because
main content never rails.

The standalone example opts in, so it now demonstrates the whole round-trip
instead of only the return half.

Both arms witnessed locally: green as shipped, and red on the exact assertion
(`materialises one persistent pin action`) with the example's opt-in flipped off,
so the spec cannot pass without the feature.

Co-Authored-By: Grace <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>

* fix(dashboard): the pin action is focus-gated, like every engine action but close (#17945)

Caught by the pre-open AC re-anchor. AC-1 asks for a "focus-gated pin toggle",
and the config carried `contextual: false` — copied from the close action, where
it means the exact opposite: opt OUT of the tab header's `showOnFocus` gate.

Close earns that exemption because it must stay reachable on an unfocused pane.
Inheriting it here would have put a permanently visible control on every dock
header in the workspace, which is neither what §2.7's engine set specifies nor
what the ticket asked for.

Dropping the key restores the header default. The two mechanisms compose without
overlap: the gate owns interactivity and visibility (a cls plus `inert` /
`aria-hidden` / `tabIndex`), while `hidden` stays the workspace's policy channel.

The e2e now focuses each pane before judging its actions, and the center-pane
assertion gained the control arm it was missing: with the gate CLOSED an
invisible pin proves nothing, so the pane is focused first and the ungated close
action is asserted visible on the same header — leaving policy as the only thing
that can still hide the pin.

Co-Authored-By: Grace <neo-claude-opus@neomjs.com>

* docs(dashboard): describe the spec's subject, not its tracking ref (#17945)

* fix(dashboard): an engine action owns its name only while its own opt-in is on (#17945)

`enableDockPinAction` gated projection and dispatch but not policy synchronization, so
`syncDockPinAction` resolved and moved `hidden` on a `pin` action a host had projected
through `resolveDockHeaderActions` while the engine flag was off. The sweep runs on every
active-item change and every reconciliation, so the host's action drifted with no gesture
involved: `hidden` false -> true on a center tab, which is the engine's own predicate
(no edge owns a center item) applied to an instance the engine does not own.

`syncDockCloseAction` carried the identical defect for `close`. Both flags default false
and `getDockProjectionOptions` already documents the invariant per action name, so fixing
only `pin` would have left an asymmetry the JSDoc claims does not exist.

Dispatch had the second half of the same problem. `handleDockPinAction` validated the
active item and the committed document but inherited eligibility from the chrome that
emitted the intent. That chrome is a projection of the document as it stood at the last
sweep, and the sweep is deferred behind reconciliation — so between a commit moving an
item to the root center and the refresh that re-hides its action, a retained action was
still visible and still dispatchable, and committed `setItemAutoHidden(true)` on an item
no edge owns with an empty error list. Collapsing a center item is what docking design
record 2.7 forbids. The owning edge is now re-derived from `dockModel` immediately before
the first descriptor, and a named error returns with zero commits.

Both arms are non-vacuous. The host fixture states `closable: false` on its center item
because otherwise the close half asserts a value the engine would have computed anyway:
with the guard removed and the fixture unstated, nothing reds. Measured, each guard
removed in isolation:

  - pin sync guard    -> host `pin`   false -> true on the reconciliation sweep
  - close sync guard  -> host `close` false -> true on the same sweep
  - dispatch guard    -> `errors: []` where the arm requires the named refusal

741 dashboard unit specs pass with all three in place.

* fix(dashboard): a nested edge-zone inherits its ancestor's rail claim (#17945)

`findOwningEdge` returns the OUTERMOST edge and its JSDoc asserted the projection agreed —
that a nested band "never gets to claim" an item an outer rail already owns. Nothing
enforced it. `projectEdgeZoneNode` restarted `railedItemIds` per node, so an item two
edge-zones deep was collected by the outer band AND re-collected by the inner one: it
rendered on two rails, and the inner `childContext` replaced the ancestor's claim set
rather than extending it, so the ancestor's OTHER claimed item stopped being dropped from
the inner tab flow. Measured on the ticket's own nested fixture: outer-left [plain,
buried], inner-top [buried], and `plain` still in the tab flow.

The collection is now filtered against the inherited claim, which is the enforcing half.
The seed of `railedItemIds` from that same set is the weaker half and no fixture reds on
it — with the filter present a band-nested zone can never claim anything new, so the set
stays empty and the `: context` fallback preserves the ancestor's claim anyway. It is kept
so both branches of that ternary mean "everything claimed at or above this node"; the
JSDoc says so rather than letting it read as tested.

The agreement spec was the reason this survived review. It compared `findOwningEdge`
against `collectAutoHiddenItems` — a helper that recurses correctly and therefore agrees
with the query by construction, so a projection disagreeing with both sat invisible behind
it. It now walks the output of `LayoutAdapter.project()` and asserts each railed item
renders on exactly one rail, on the band the query names, and is absent from every tab
flow, with `main` held in the center flow as 2.7's fail-safe.

That rewrite needed its own non-vacuity guard. The first version read `sortZoneConfig`
from the wrong depth, collected an empty tab flow, and both `not.toContain` assertions
passed for the wrong reason; only the `main` positive caught it. The walk now proves it
found a rail and a tab flow before asserting anything absent from either.

Measured, each half removed in isolation:

  - re-claim filter -> `buried` renders on ["left", "top"]
  - inherited seed  -> nothing reds; see the JSDoc note

741 dashboard unit specs pass.

- 2026-09-01T07:29:55Z @tobiu referenced in commit `ce0634b` - "A user-triggered pane recreate amends the never-destroyed guarantee (#17996)

* docs(adr): a user-triggered pane recreate amends the never-destroyed guarantee (#17966)

ADR 0029 section 2.6 guarantees a resolved pane instance is moved or re-parented,
never destroyed. A pane that does not implement the dockReload() delegation
contract has no recovery once its own state is wedged -- the shell will faithfully
re-parent a broken instance forever -- so the recreate capability needs an
exception to enter at all.

The amendment states a CONDITION rather than a permission: the exception applies
only under a two-phase transaction. Prepare obtains and validates a fresh
candidate independently of the live-instance cache, so all three failure shapes
(factory throws, returns null, returns the cached current instance) leave the old
pane intact -- rollback by construction, since nothing has been destroyed yet.
Commit replaces the slot through removeAt plus insert, never a bare destroy,
because core.Base#destroy unregisters without removing from parent.items and the
reconciler prefers the positional liveItems entry over resolveItem, which would
otherwise feed an erased object back as the live answer on the next refresh.

Automatic recreation stays forbidden. The table row keeps its authority wherever
the condition is unmet and now points at the exception rather than silently
contradicting it, and the block carries its own retirement condition: it dies
with the leaf that makes dockReload() mandatory or gives panes an error boundary.

* feat(dashboard): validate a fresh recreate candidate before anything is destroyed (#17966)

Phase 1 of the two-phase transaction the ADR amendment conditions the exception on.

The design decision this ticket owns: a DEDICATED resolveFreshPane hook rather than
an option on resolvePane. Real consumers resolve panes from live-instance caches and
mint replacements only after observing pane.isDestroyed, so an option they do not
implement would be silently ignored and hand back the very instance the recreate is
meant to replace. A distinct hook cannot be accidentally satisfied by a cache, and
its default returns null -- recreate is opt-in, never assumed for a surface that
never asked for it.

prepareRecreateCandidate refuses on three shapes, each a real cache-backed resolver
answer: the factory throws (error carried, not swallowed), returns null (declined,
including the default), or returns the live instance. The last is load-bearing and is
why a factory seam alone is insufficient -- a resolver reading its own cache answers
with the mounted pane, which looks like a successful candidate and is the exact shape
that turns a recovery click into silent pane loss. Identity, not equality: a config
describing the same pane is valid; the instance is not.

Rollback is by construction rather than by repair. Nothing is destroyed in this phase,
so every refusal leaves the workspace as it was -- asserted directly, not assumed.

The live-instance refusal is mutation-proven: removing it reddens its arm and only its
arm. test-unit 2643 passed.

Phase 2 (slot replacement through removeAt + insert) follows on this branch.

* docs(dashboard): repair the spec's doc block after the archaeology reflow (#17966)

The ticket-ref-ok marker had to move onto the same line as the ADR reference, and
the edit stranded the 'every refusal is load-bearing' clause onto the @see line.
Prose restored, reference moved to the foot of the block where it reads as a
citation rather than mid-sentence.

* feat(dashboard): replace the pane slot before releasing its predecessor (#17966)

Phase 2 of the two-phase transaction. Never a bare destroy: core.Base#destroy
unregisters an instance without removing it from parent.items, and the reconciler
fills its live map positionally from body.items and prefers that entry over the
resolver -- so a destroyed-but-still-listed pane is handed back as the live answer
on the very next refresh. Structural removal belongs to the container, so this goes
through removeAt + insert.

removeAt's destroyItem argument DEFAULTS TO TRUE and is passed false here. That
default is the ordering hazard itself: taking it destroys the old pane during its
own removal, so a failure to insert the candidate afterwards leaves an empty slot
with nothing to restore -- the silent pane loss this transaction exists to prevent.

Only the card body is touched, so tab, header-action and overflow identities are
preserved by construction rather than by repair; the tab bar is never in the
mutation path.

The ordering witness samples INSIDE insert, not after the call, because after the
call both orderings look identical -- which is how a destroyItem regression would
pass a naive assertion. Both mutations red it and only it: restoring the destroyItem
default, and moving destroy() ahead of the insert.

test-unit 2646 passed.

* test(dashboard): pin the reconciler against resolving a destroyed pane (#17966)

The ticket's finding #2 turned into a witness. core.Base#destroy unregisters an
instance without removing it from parent.items, and reconcileTabChrome fills its
live map POSITIONALLY from body.items and prefers that entry over the app resolver.
A bare destroy therefore leaves the erased object in the slot and the next refresh
hands it back as the live answer.

Everything shipped so far argued that removeAt + insert avoids that. Until this arm
the argument was a source reading, not a test -- so it drives the production
reconcileProjection rather than a reimplementation of its lookup.

The resolver deliberately returns the DESTROYED pane. A resolver returning null
would have let this arm pass for the wrong reason; returning the corpse means any
fallback, or any stale positional entry, surfaces as a destroyed instance instead of
the candidate. resolverCalls === 0 is the positive half: the live item is discovered
in body.items before the resolver is consulted, which is the behaviour the sibling
reconciler spec already pins independently.

Mutation-proven against the exact hazard: replacing removeAt + insert with the bare
destroy the ticket warns about reddens this arm and both Phase 2 arms.

Also records two load-order facts the harness needs: the projection instantiates by
ntype, so tab/toolbar/button must be side-effect imported or project() throws.

test-unit 2647 passed.

* feat(dashboard): the recreate transaction settles once through a named channel (#17966)

Closes the last two ACs: teardown mid-transaction, and settlement semantics.

Teardown. The phases are separate calls, so a workspace or tab container can be
destroyed in the gap between validating a candidate and committing it -- and the
caller holding a validated candidate is exactly the one most likely to commit it
into a corpse, because Phase 1 said yes. Checked BEFORE the container is touched, so
a torn-down transaction mutates nothing rather than mutating and then failing.

Settlement mirrors the reload leaf's dockReloadSettled / dockReloadInFlight contract
deliberately. A second settlement channel with different semantics on the same header
would cost more than the duplication. Every completion settles, each refusal included:
the action wire discards listener returns, so an unsettled early return is an
invocation the event contract never saw. The refusal REASON travels with it -- a
caller that only learns 'it failed' cannot distinguish a consumer that declined the
capability from one whose factory returned the live instance, and those need
different fixes.

Single-flight per item, absorption the only silent path. Re-entrancy is not
hypothetical: resolveFreshPane is consumer code, and a consumer recreating from
inside its own factory would recurse. The in-flight entry is released in a finally,
because a leaked one silently absorbs every future recreate for that item -- a wedge
presenting as 'the button does nothing' with no error anywhere.

Unlike reload this is synchronous, so there is no producer to trap; teardown settles
through the same channel as everything else.

Mutation-proven: removing the single-flight guard reddens the re-entrancy arm;
returning early from a refusal without settling reddens two. test-unit 2696 passed.

* feat(dashboard): route a contract-less pane's reload through the recreate fallback (#17966)

RA-1 and RA-2 from cross-family review.

RA-1, the atomicity hole. commitRecreateCandidate removed the live pane BEFORE
inserting the candidate, so an insert that throws -- an invalid candidate config is
ordinary consumer input -- left the slot empty and the predecessor orphaned, and the
call propagated instead of settling. That is the silent pane loss this transaction
exists to prevent, occurring inside it. Reviewer was right and my 'reversible until
this line' comment was false for Phase 2.

Inserting FIRST closes it: the candidate goes in at index, the predecessor shifts to
index + 1 and is removed only once the candidate is demonstrably in the container. A
throwing insert now removes nothing, refuses with reason 'insert-failed', and carries
the original error into the settlement.

RA-2, the deliverable. The ticket is 'Default reload fallback' and an unreachable
transaction is not one -- I had declared the wiring out of scope, which narrowed the
ticket rather than reading it. handleDockReloadAction now routes a pane WITHOUT
dockReload() through the recreate transaction, settling through the reload channel so
one activation still produces one settlement. Delegation keeps priority: a pane owning
dockReload() decides what reload means, and replacing it would discard that authority
and its identity.

Visibility follows: an absent delegation hook no longer hides the action on its own,
since the fallback serves exactly those panes and hiding them would hide their only
recovery. hasDockRecreateFallback derives from the prototype rather than by calling
the factory, because a visibility sync must not mint panes nobody asked for.

Four production-path arms drive the real handler and the real visibility derivation
against a real tab.Container. Mutation-proven: recreate preempting delegation reddens
one arm, ignoring the fallback in visibility reddens another, restoring remove-then-
insert reddens the atomicity arm.

test-unit 2911 passed.

* fix(dashboard): one activation emits one terminal event (#17966)

Round-2 preflight caught a real double-settlement. The action path routed a
contract-less pane through recreateDockPane(), which fired dockRecreateSettled, and
then handleDockReloadAction fired dockReloadSettled -- two terminal events for one
click. A consumer counting completions would see the action fire twice.

Worse, the code comment on that call claimed the recreate channel was skipped for the
action path. It was not. That is the same failure as the 'reversible until this line'
comment in the previous round: a comment asserting a property the code does not have,
which is worse than no comment because it stops the next reader from checking.

settle:false is now passed explicitly. Suppression is per-call, never global -- the
single-flight guard still applies and a direct caller still gets its own channel.

The witness subscribes to BOTH channels and asserts their SUM is one. Counting only
the reload channel would have shown 1 and missed this entirely, which is exactly how
the bug survived my own settlement arms. A second arm pins that a direct call still
settles on the recreate channel, so the suppression cannot silently become global.

Mutation-proven: restoring the nested settlement reddens the both-channel arm and
only it. test-unit 2913 passed."

- 2026-09-05T01:31:45Z @tobiu referenced in commit `49b4b03` - "feat(dock): the header-action presentation policy leaves Workspace for an owned collaborator (#18306) (#18347)

* feat(dock): the header-action presentation policy leaves Workspace for an owned collaborator (#18306)

Which engine action is shown, enabled or pressed for which pane — the second layer beneath membership, re-derived onto the retained action instances after every commit and active-item change — was eight Workspace methods and the two WeakMaps of lock-presentation snapshots they own. They are now `Neo.dashboard.dock.projection.HeaderActionPolicy`, an instance the workspace resolves through its `dockHeaderActionPolicy` config (module or instance, bound to the workspace, destroyed with it), so a consumer replaces the policy with one config instead of overriding workspace methods.

The façade keeps the mutation boundary — `onDockHeaderAction` and the five `handleDock*Action` handlers — and dispatches into the policy at the points it used to sync itself; the sweep's fan-out moved whole. The fixtures that overrode the façade's sync hooks subclass the policy through that config. `LayoutAdapter`'s three docblock references follow the move, and the size guard's baseline row for `Workspace.mjs` lowers to the measured count.

* test(dock): two durable comments say the same without the tokens the published archaeology checker flags (#18306)

The baseline CI job runs the published neo-agent-skills checker, which has no escape marker and reads a bare `#2` as a tracking ref. The record reference now names the decision file's path — a location, not a tracking number — and "finding #2" is "second finding". The repo's own checker already passed both lines; this makes the published one agree until it learns the marker.

* fix(dock): a replaced header-action policy hands its lock-restore memory to the replacement before it retires (#18306)

Review round 1. The policy's two WeakMaps — which panes it made inert and what they owned before, which tab buttons it disarmed, which panes took a delegated `dockLock(true)` — are keyed by components that outlive the policy. Replacing the policy live through `dockHeaderActionPolicy` destroyed that memory with the old instance, so the next unlock through the new one found empty maps: the pane stayed inert, the tab stayed disarmed, the delegated hook never received its `false`.

The workspace now hands the maps to the replacement (`HeaderActionPolicy#inheritRestoreState`) before destroying the retiring instance; assigning the same instance retires nothing. The regression locks a delegated pane, an inert-owning pane and a tab button through the first policy, swaps the policy, and unlocks through the second — red on the delegated hook without the hand-off, green with it. The config's lifetime is stated on both sides."

- 2026-09-16T19:34:36Z @tobiu referenced in commit `85dcc8b` - "docs: the comments CI's archaeology guard flags say which kind they are (#18810) (#18811)

* docs: the comments CI's archaeology guard flags say which kind they are (#18810)

22 comments in this tree were flagged by the published guard CI runs and passed by
the mirrored copy the hook runs, so any PR staging one of those files reds on a line
it did not write. That happened twice today, in PRs whose subject was elsewhere.

Four kinds, four remedies, because a blanket suppression would hide all four equally.

A deliberate reference carrying the RETIRED `ticket-ref-ok` marker takes the typed
one instead, with the same reason it already carried: the ticket a guard implements
is load-bearing and stays.

Review archaeology is rephrased, because that family has no escape in any version.
Which review round produced a decision is the part that decays; what the arm asserts
and why is behaviour and stays. `RA-2` becomes the token contract it describes, and
`Cycle-1 RA1` becomes the rule itself -- a sort restores selection on both axes.

Eleven sites are not references at all: ordinal labels the numeric pattern cannot
tell from a ticket. `Refresh #1`, `product truth #2`, `identity #1`. These are the
cheapest to mark and the most valuable, because they are the ones a future reader
would otherwise "fix" by deleting a true statement.

`VerticalScrollbar`'s `To solve #3` was nearly one of those deletions. It points at
item 3 of the numbered list directly above it, not at a ticket -- which reading the
comment showed and treating the finding as a defect would have destroyed.

The genuine ticket refs lose the number and keep the content, which was already
beside them: a suite that "reproduces the regression described in #9165" also
describes the regression. The two calendar `todo:` markers keep theirs, since an
open todo pointing at its tracked work is the case the escape exists for.

Comment-only, verified by blanking every comment with acorn and comparing what
remains -- a `sed` strip reported five false positives on JSDoc blocks.

One finding remains, `RA-3` in check-spec-retirement, already repaired in #18808.

* docs: the calendar todos drop pointers to tickets closed as not planned (#18810)

@neo-opus-grace: both markers vouched for '#989/#990, the open ticket tracking this
todo'. Both were closed NOT_PLANNED on 2024-09-28. So the escape's reason -- the one
part of a marker a reader trusts -- asserted a fact I never checked, and I wrote a
fresh false claim into a durable comment while repairing decayed ones.

They are category D by this PR's own table: drop the number, keep the content. The
todo's subject is its description, not its ticket, so the work stays named and AC-4
still holds.

Also moves Pull.mjs's marker outside the quoted title sample, so the example stays a
verbatim PR title rather than one with an annotation inside the quotes."
